context: Mia meets Noah at the community center and asks for his phone number.
Could I have your number? I will call you about the English class.
dialogue: Hello, Noah. I am Mia. We are in the same English class.
Hello, Mia. It is nice to meet you. Do you live near here?
Yes, I live on Green Street. Could I have your number, please? I want to call you about our homework.
Of course. My number is 909-555-0148. The area code is 909.
Thank you. How can I reach you after six? I am at work in the afternoon.
You can reach me on my smartphone after six. I will save your number too.
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Noah for his phone number. Say why you want it.
lessons.goal: I can ask for someone’s phone number and say how to reach me.
lessons.listening: Mia meets Noah at the community center. She asks for his phone number and the area code. Noah gives her his number, and Mia saves it on her smartphone. She will call him about the English class on Monday.

mainWord.definition: A phone that can use the internet and apps.
mainWord.example: Bella calls Fenrir on her smartphone.

lessons.mainWordForms: Smartphone is a noun. The plural is smartphones. We call or text on a smartphone. A smartphone is a phone, a camera, and a small computer in one.
lessons.model: Could I have your number? You can reach me on my smartphone.

newItems.definition: A phone that can use the internet and apps.
newItems.example: Bella calls Fenrir on her smartphone.

newItems.definition: The first numbers of a phone number for one area.
newItems.example: The area code for this city is 909.

newItems.definition: A polite way to ask for someone’s phone number.
newItems.example: Could I have your number, please?

newItems.definition: A direct way to ask for someone’s phone number.
newItems.example: What’s your number? I will call you tomorrow.

newItems.definition: A polite way to ask for the best way to contact someone.
newItems.example: How can I reach you after six?

lessons.other: The time of the English class
lessons.question: What does Mia save on her smartphone?
lessons.reading: Mia meets Noah at the community center on Monday. She wants his phone number, so she asks, “Could I have your number, please?” Noah smiles and says, “Of course. My number is 909-555-0148, and the area code is 909.” Mia asks, “What’s your number again? I want to save it.” Noah repeats the number slowly. Then Mia asks, “How can I reach you after six?” Noah answers, “You can reach me on my smartphone. I always have it with me.” Mia saves the number and says, “Thank you. I will call you about the English class.”
lessons.readingA: She asks Noah for his phone number and the area code.
lessons.readingQ: What does Mia ask Noah for?
lessons.sound: Smartphone has its strongest beat on SMART. In area code, say AREA clearly. In could I have your number, say NUMBER clearly at the end.
lessons.speaking: Tell a partner how to reach you. Give your phone number with the area code, and say the best time to call you.
lessons.speakingSample: My name is Mia, and my number is 909-555-0148. The area code is 909. You can reach me on my smartphone after six in the evening. Please call me about the English class, and I will answer. If I do not answer, please leave a short message.
lessons.title: Ask for a name and a phone number
lessons.use: Ask for someone’s phone number in a polite, friendly way.
lessons.wordSample: She calls her friend on her smartphone.
lessons.wordTask: What does Bella use to call Fenrir?
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words to a new friend. Ask for their phone number and area code, and say how they can reach you and the best time to call.
lessons.writingSample: Hello, Noah. It is nice to meet you in our English class. Could I have your number, please? I want to call you about our homework. What is the area code for your city? Mine is 909. How can I reach you after six? You can reach me on my smartphone in the evening. Please call me, and I will answer.

context: Noah writes his last name, Smith-Jones, on a form.
Could you spell that? I want to write it letter by letter.
lessons.correct: Noah’s last name, letter by letter
dialogue: Noah, I need your last name for the class list. Could you spell that, please?
Of course. It is S-M-I-T-H hyphen J-O-N-E-S. Please write it letter by letter.
Thank you. Is there an apostrophe in your first name?
No, there is not. My first name is Noah, N-O-A-H. Can you sound it out with me?
Yes. N-O-A-H. Noah. And Smith-Jones has a hyphen. I will write it now.
That is right. Thank you for writing it carefully.
lessons.example: There is a hyphen in my name.
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Noah to spell his last name. Say that you want to write it letter by letter.
lessons.goal: I can ask someone to spell a name or a word and write the letters down.
lessons.grammar: There is a hyphen in my name
lessons.listening: Noah writes his last name on a form. His last name is Smith-Jones, with a hyphen between Smith and Jones. Bella asks him to spell it letter by letter. Noah says the letters slowly, and Bella writes them down.

mainWord.definition: A short line (-) between parts of a word or name.
mainWord.example: There is a hyphen in my last name, Smith-Jones.

lessons.mainWordForms: Hyphen is a noun. The plural is hyphens. A hyphen joins two parts of a name or a word, like Smith-Jones. We do not say the hyphen; we say the letters around it.
lessons.model: My last name is Smith-Jones. There is a hyphen in it.

newItems.definition: A short line (-) between parts of a word or name.
newItems.example: There is a hyphen in my last name, Smith-Jones.

newItems.definition: The mark (’) in a word like O’Brien or don’t.
newItems.example: The apostrophe in O’Brien comes after the O.

newItems.definition: One letter at a time, slowly.
newItems.example: Please say your name letter by letter.

newItems.definition: A polite way to ask someone to spell a word.
newItems.example: Could you spell that word for me?

newItems.definition: Say a word slowly, sound by sound.
newItems.example: Sound it out, and I will write the letters.

There is a hyphen between Smith and Jones.” Bella writes the name letter by letter. Then she asks about his friend O’Brien. “Is there an apostrophe in O’Brien?” Noah answers, “Yes, the apostrophe comes after the O.” Bella says, “Please sound it out for me.” Noah says the letters slowly, and Bella writes them down.
lessons.readingA: There is a hyphen between Smith and Jones.
lessons.readingQ: What mark is in Noah’s last name?
lessons.sound: Hyphen has its strongest beat on HY. In apostrophe, say STRO clearly. In letter by letter, say each word slowly, with a clear LETTER.
lessons.speaking: Tell a partner how to spell your first name and last name. Say the letters slowly, letter by letter, and say if there is a hyphen or an apostrophe.
lessons.speakingSample: My first name is Mia, M-I-A. My last name is Reed, R-E-E-D. There is no hyphen in my name, and there is no apostrophe. Please write it letter by letter. Could you spell that back to me? I want to check that you have it right.
lessons.task: There is a hyphen ___ my name.
lessons.title: Ask someone to spell a name or a word
lessons.use: Ask someone to spell a name or a word when you do not know the letters.
lessons.wordSample: My last name has a hyphen in it.
lessons.wordTask: What mark joins the two parts of Smith-Jones?
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words about your name. Spell your first name and last name, and say if there is a hyphen or an apostrophe in it.
lessons.writingSample: My name is Mia Reed. My first name is Mia, M-I-A. My last name is Reed, R-E-E-D. There is no hyphen in my name, and there is no apostrophe. Please write it letter by letter. Could you spell that back to me? I want to make sure you have the right spelling.

context: Bella wants to visit Fenrir at his home this weekend.
What is the street address? I also need the apartment number.
dialogue: Fenrir, I want to visit you this weekend. What is the street address?
It is 24 Green Street, in the north district. My apartment number is 12B.
Thank you. Is your home on the top floor of the building?
No, my home is on the third floor. The top floor has the reading room.
Good. What is the house number again? Is it 24?
Yes, the house number is 24. I will meet you at the door on Saturday.
lessons.example: What is the street address of the library?
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Fenrir for the street address of his home and the apartment number.
lessons.goal: I can ask for an address and find the place.
lessons.grammar: What is the street address of the library?
lessons.listening: Bella wants to visit the new library in the north district. She asks Fenrir for the street address. The library is at 24 Green Street, and the class room is on the top floor. Fenrir also gives her his apartment number, 12B.

mainWord.definition: One part of a city or town.
mainWord.example: The library is in the north district of the city.

lessons.mainWordForms: District is a noun. The plural is districts. A city has many districts. We say the name of a district to help people find a place.
lessons.model: The library is in the north district. What is the street address?

newItems.definition: One part of a city or town.
newItems.example: The library is in the north district of the city.

newItems.definition: The house number and street name of a place.
newItems.example: What is the street address of the library?

newItems.definition: The number of one home in a building.
newItems.example: My apartment number is 12B.

newItems.definition: The number of a house on a street.
newItems.example: The house number is 24.

newItems.definition: The highest floor in a building.
newItems.example: The class is on the top floor.

lessons.pattern: What is the + noun + of + place
lessons.question: Where is the class room in the library?
lessons.reading: Bella wants to visit Fenrir at his home this weekend. She asks, “What is the street address?” Fenrir answers, “It is 24 Green Street, in the north district. My apartment number is 12B.” Bella asks, “What is the house number again?” Fenrir says, “The house number is 24.” Bella also asks about the top floor. Fenrir says, “My home is on the third floor. The top floor has the reading room.” Bella writes the address down and says, “Thank you. I will come on Saturday.”
lessons.sound: District has its strongest beat on DIS. In street address, say STREET clearly. In top floor, say TOP clearly so the listener hears the highest floor.
lessons.speaking: Tell a partner your street address and apartment number. Say the district, the house number, and the floor of your home.
lessons.speakingSample: I live at 24 Green Street, in the north district of the city. My apartment number is 12B, on the third floor. The house number is 24. The building is near the library. Please come on Saturday. The reading room is on the top floor, next to the big window.
lessons.task: What is the street address ___ the library?
lessons.title: Ask for an address and find the place
lessons.use: Ask for the address of a place you want to visit.
lessons.wordSample: The library is in the north district.
lessons.wordTask: Which part of the city is the library in?
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words to a friend. Give your street address and apartment number, and say the district and the floor of your home.
lessons.writingSample: Hello, Fenrir. Please come to my home on Saturday. My street address is 24 Green Street, in the north district. My apartment number is 12B, on the third floor. The house number is 24. The building is near the library. The reading room is on the top floor, next to the big window. I will meet you at the door.

context: Bella missed the English class on Monday. She meets Fenrir on Tuesday.
What time does it start? I want to come on Friday.
dialogue: Fenrir, I missed the English class on Monday. Did I miss anything?
No, we only talked about the new book. What day is it today? It is Tuesday.
Thank you. What time does it start on Friday?
It starts at ten in the morning. When does it start for you? Is ten too early?
No, ten is good. Is the library closed on Sunday?
Yes, it is closed on Sunday, but it is open on Friday. See you then.
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Fenrir what time the English class starts on Friday and what day it is.
lessons.goal: I can ask for the time or date of an event I missed.
lessons.listening: Bella missed the English class on Monday. On Tuesday, she meets Fenrir and asks about the class. The class starts at ten on Friday in the library. The library is closed on Sunday, but it is open on Friday.

mainWord.definition: Not open; you cannot go in.
mainWord.example: The library is closed on Sunday.

lessons.mainWordForms: Closed is an adjective. The verb is close. A shop is closed when people cannot go in. The opposite is open.
lessons.model: The library is closed on Sunday. What time does it start on Friday?

newItems.definition: Not open; you cannot go in.
newItems.example: The library is closed on Sunday.

newItems.definition: A way to ask for the start time of an event.
newItems.example: What time does it start on Friday?

newItems.definition: A way to ask for the day or time an event starts.
newItems.example: When does it start? I want to come.

newItems.definition: A way to ask for the day of an event.
newItems.example: What day is it? I forgot the date.

newItems.definition: A way to ask if something important happened.
newItems.example: Did I miss anything in the class?

lessons.pattern: What time does it + base verb
lessons.question: When does the English class start?
lessons.reading: Bella missed the English class on Monday. On Tuesday, she meets Fenrir. She asks, “Did I miss anything?” Fenrir says, “No, we only talked about the new book.” Bella asks, “What day is it today?” Fenrir answers, “It is Tuesday.” Then Bella asks, “What time does it start on Friday?” Fenrir says, “It starts at ten. When does it start for you?” Bella says, “Ten is good. Is the library closed on Sunday?” Fenrir answers, “Yes, it is closed on Sunday, but it is open on Friday.”
lessons.readingA: It starts at ten in the morning.
lessons.readingQ: What time does the English class start on Friday?
lessons.sound: Closed has its strongest beat on CLOSED. In what time does it start, say TIME clearly. In did I miss anything, say MISS clearly.
lessons.speaking: Tell a partner about a class you missed. Ask what time it starts, what day it is, and if you missed anything important.
lessons.speakingSample: I missed the English class on Monday, and I want to know what happened. Did I miss anything important? What time does it start on Friday? When does it start in the morning? Is the library closed on Sunday? I will come on Friday at ten, and I will bring my book.
lessons.title: Ask for a time or a date you missed
lessons.use: Ask for the time or day of an event you missed.
lessons.wordSample: The library is closed on Sunday.
lessons.wordTask: Is the library open or closed on Sunday?
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words to a friend. Say you missed a class, and ask what time it starts, what day it is, and if you missed anything.
lessons.writingSample: Hello, Fenrir. I missed the English class on Monday, and I want to know what happened. Did I miss anything important? What time does it start on Friday? When does it start in the morning? What day is it today? Is the library closed on Sunday? I will come on Friday at ten. Please tell me if I need to bring my book.

context: Fenrir speaks fast, and Bella does not hear the time of the class.
Could you repeat that? Please say it clearly.
dialogue: Fenrir, what time does the class start? I didn’t catch that.
It starts at ten on Friday. Did you hear me?
Could you repeat that, please? Say that again, slowly.
Of course. It starts at ten on Friday. Tell me if I speak too fast.
Thank you. Please speak clearly. I want to write the time down.
Good. Ten on Friday. I will speak up so you can hear me.
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Fenrir to repeat the time of the class. Ask him to say it clearly.
lessons.goal: I can ask someone to repeat something slowly and clearly.
lessons.listening: Fenrir tells Bella the time of the English class, but he speaks fast. Bella says she did not catch the time. Fenrir repeats it slowly and clearly: the class starts at ten on Friday. Bella writes the time down and thanks him.

mainWord.definition: In a way that is easy to hear and understand.
mainWord.example: Please speak clearly so I can understand you.

lessons.mainWordForms: Clearly is an adverb. The adjective is clear. Speak clearly means speak in a way that people can hear and understand. We say speak clearly and write clearly.
lessons.model: Could you repeat that, please? Say it clearly.

newItems.definition: In a way that is easy to hear and understand.
newItems.example: Please speak clearly so I can understand you.

newItems.definition: A polite way to ask someone to say something again.
newItems.example: Could you repeat that, please? I did not hear you.

newItems.definition: A way to ask someone to say something one more time.
newItems.example: Say that again, please. I want to hear it one more time.

newItems.definition: A polite way to say you did not hear or understand.
newItems.example: I didn’t catch that. Could you repeat it?

newItems.definition: Speak louder so people can hear you.
newItems.example: Please speak up. I cannot hear you at the back.

lessons.question: What time does the English class start?
lessons.reading: Fenrir tells Bella the time of the English class, but he speaks fast. Bella says, “I didn’t catch that. Could you repeat that, please?” Fenrir says the time again, slowly and clearly: ten on Friday. Bella asks, “Say that again, please.” Fenrir repeats it and says, “I will speak up so you can hear me.” Bella smiles and says, “Thank you. Now I can hear you clearly.”
lessons.readingA: She asks him to repeat the time slowly and clearly.
lessons.readingQ: What does Bella ask Fenrir to do?
lessons.sound: Clearly has its strongest beat on CLEAR. In could you repeat that, say REPEAT clearly. In speak up, say UP clearly so the listener hears it.
lessons.speaking: Tell a partner that you did not hear something. Ask them to repeat it slowly and clearly, and say the time or number back.
lessons.speakingSample: I didn’t catch that. Could you repeat that, please? Say that again, slowly and clearly. The class starts at ten on Friday, is that right? Please speak up a little. I want to write the time down and check it with you.
lessons.title: Ask someone to repeat slowly and clearly
lessons.use: Ask someone to say something again, slowly and clearly.
lessons.wordSample: Please speak clearly so I can understand you.
lessons.wordTask: How should Bella speak so Fenrir can understand her?
lessons.writing: Write 45–65 words to a friend. Say you did not hear the time of a class, and ask them to repeat it slowly and clearly.
lessons.writingSample: Hello, Fenrir. I didn’t catch that. Could you repeat that, please? Say that again, slowly and clearly. What time does the class start? Is it ten on Friday? Please speak up a little. I want to write the time down. Thank you for saying it clearly. I will come on Friday at ten.

context: Bella calls Fenrir, but he does not answer. She hears a beep.
Please call me back. This is urgent. My number is 909-555-0173.
dialogue: Fenrir, I called you this morning, but you did not answer.
Sorry, I missed your call. I was in class. What did your message say?
I said it is urgent. Please call me back after six.
Of course. I will call you back after six. Can you take a message for Noah?
Yes. What should I tell him?
Tell him the class starts at ten. Thank you for taking the message.
lessons.example: Please call me back after six.
lessons.expressionTask: Leave a message for Fenrir. Say it is urgent, ask him to call you back, and give your number.
lessons.goal: I can leave a message with the missing details.
lessons.grammar: Please call me back after six
lessons.listening: Bella calls Fenrir, but he does not answer. She hears a beep and leaves a short message. She says it is urgent and asks Fenrir to call her back after six. She gives her number, 909-555-0173. Fenrir hears the message later.

mainWord.definition: A short sound on a phone, after which you can speak.
mainWord.example: Please leave a message after the beep.

lessons.mainWordForms: Beep is a noun. The plural is beeps. A phone makes a beep sound. After the beep, you can leave a message.
lessons.model: Please leave a message after the beep. This is urgent.

newItems.definition: A short sound on a phone, after which you can speak.
newItems.example: Please leave a message after the beep.

newItems.definition: Very important; it needs a fast answer.
newItems.example: This is urgent. Please call me back today.

newItems.definition: Phone me again later.

lessons.question: What does Bella ask Fenrir to do?
lessons.reading: Bella calls Fenrir in the morning, but he does not answer. She hears a beep and leaves a short message: “Hello, Fenrir. This is Bella. This is urgent. Please call me back after six. My number is 909-555-0173.” Fenrir hears the message later. He says, “Sorry, I missed your call. I was in class.” He calls Bella back and asks, “Can you take a message for Noah?” Bella says, “Yes. Tell me what to say.”
lessons.readingA: She asks him to call her back after six.
lessons.readingQ: What does Bella ask Fenrir to do in her message?

lessons.speaking: Tell a partner about a call you missed. Leave a short message: say it is urgent, ask them to call you back, and give your number.
lessons.speakingSample: Hello, Fenrir. This is Bella. I called you this morning, but you did not answer. This is urgent. Please call me back after six. My number is 909-555-0173. Thank you for calling me back.

lessons.use: Leave a short message when someone does not answer the phone.
lessons.wordSample: Please leave a message after the beep.

context: Bella writes down the time of the class: ten on Friday.
Did I get that right? The class is at ten on Friday.
lessons.correct: The time and the address of the class
dialogue: Fenrir, did you mention the time of the class? I want to say it back to you.
Yes. The class is at ten on Friday. Please say it back.
Ten on Friday. Did I get that right?
Yes, that is right. Do you mind if I ask you to check the address too?
No, I do not mind. I will look it up on my smartphone.
Thank you. The address is 24 Green Street. Please say it back to me.
lessons.expressionTask: Say the time of the class back to Fenrir and ask if it is right.
lessons.goal: I can check the details I heard by saying them back.
lessons.listening: Bella checks the details of the English class. She says the time back to Fenrir: ten on Friday. She asks, “Did I get that right?” Fenrir says yes. Then Bella looks up the address and says it back too.

lessons.model: Did you mention the time? The class is at ten. Did I get that right?

lessons.wordSample: Did you mention the time of the class?

lessons.writingSample: Hello, Fenrir. Did you mention the time of the class? The class is at ten on Friday. Did I get that right? The address is 24 Green Street. Did I get that right too? I will say it back to you. Do you mind if I look it up on my smartphone? Thank you for your help.

context: Mia phones the Riverside Community Center about a free English class.
Could you tell me more? I need the day, the time, and the address.
dialogue: Mia phoned the community center today. She asked about the free English class.
Good. Could you tell me more? What did Ms. Reed say?
The class is on Monday at eleven, at 24 Green Street. Mia needs the address.
That helps a lot. Monday at eleven. Did Mia ask what to bring?
Yes. Ms. Reed said to bring a notebook and a pen. Mia can’t wait to start.
Thanks for the information. That’s all I need. I will come too.
lessons.example: Could you tell me more about the class?
lessons.expressionTask: Ask Ms. Reed for more information about the English class: the day, the time, and the address.
lessons.goal: I can ask for missing information and check it in a new situation.
lessons.grammar: Could you tell me more about the class?

mainWord.definition: A polite way to ask for more information.
mainWord.example: Could you tell me more about the English class?
